title: protocol-harmonizer-for-openai-responses-parity-mitigation
creator: Anika Rao
description: We need a pragmatic, low-risk compatibility layer that maps OpenAI Responses semantics to Redwood's Responses-compatible runtime behaviors. This ticket scopes a design and an implementable shim (the Protocol Harmonizer) that reduces observed parity gaps for streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs while minimizing behavioral regressions for existing customers.
problem_statement: Field reports and internal audits show three recurring failure modes when routing OpenAI Responses-style traffic through our runtime: (1) loss or reordering of streaming events that breaks client incremental parsing, (2) tool/function call boundary mismatches (argument types, partial args mid-stream, and ambiguous end-of-call markers), and (3) structured output schema drift where models emit JSON fragments that differ in tokenization boundaries and escape sequences compared to our canonical parser. These lead to customer errors, flaky tests, and unclear telemetry.
proposed_solution: Build a Protocol Harmonizer module that lives in the request path and performs lightweight transformation and reconciliation: (a) a streaming event canonicalizer that timestamps and sequence-numbers inbound fragments and emits normalized chunk events to the client stream, (b) a tool-call composer that buffers function-call tokens until a deterministic complete-arg boundary is observed (falling back to best-effort heuristics with explicit flags when streaming cutpoints occur), and (c) a tolerant structured-output adapter that runs a set of schema-aware repairing passes (escape normalization, trailing-comma handling, and partial-json stitching) before handing results to downstream SDKs. The harmonizer should be configurable per-deployment and opt-in via a top-level compatibility flag for canarying.
acceptance_criteria: A deployable harmonizer proof-of-concept that can be toggled per-model-route
End-to-end tests demonstrating <1% increase in median latency for small requests and no >5% regressions on 99th percentile in our canary pool

Client-facing behavior parity tests: accepted corpus of 120 representative Responses transcripts where the harmonizer produces semantically equivalent outputs for 95% of cases compared to our reference mapping
Failure-mode telemetry: clear signal emitted when heuristics are used, including example fragment dumps for offline analysis
Canary rollout plan and rollback logic documented in the runbook
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Laboratory - implement POC and run corpus-driven synthetic tests (local)
Phase 1: Internal canary - enable for internal customers and internal integration tests only
Phase 2: External opt-in - route 1% of new traffic for customers who opt in to the compatibility flag
Phase 3: Observability gating - extend to 10% where metrics meet thresholds, then 50%
Phase 4: Default off - keep off by default for 2025-Q2; escalate to default-on only after cross-team sign-off
telemetry_and_metrics: metric:compat.harmonizer.used_count - how many requests touched the harmonizer
metric:compat.harmonizer.heuristic_count - number of heuristic repairs performed
event:compat.harmonizer.example_dump - sampled payload dump to S3 for triage (scrubbed)
decision_log: 2025-02-28: Chose buffered deterministic boundaries over naive token-count heuristics to reduce tool-call truncation errors (agreed by runtime and SDK leads).
2025-03-01: Decided harmonizer will be a pluggable middleware rather than baked into kernel-level serving to allow rapid iteration and canary toggles.
